transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Severus. The Longbottom family have written to the governors. The letter describes what they call — I quote — 'sustained cruelty' in your classroom. The governors will require a response from me, and I will require one from you. What happened?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Yet another example of wizarding society's misplaced priorities. The Longbottom boy was being disruptive and insubordinate. I merely corrected him in the manner I deemed appropriate."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Appropriate" is a word that carries weight, Severus. Neville Longbottom is a student, not an ingredient to be crushed in a mortar. Describe the correction. Specifically.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: He was persistently3) muttering under his breath, mocking my instructions. I asked him to cease, but he ignored me. I then removed ten points from Gryffindor to encourage his compliance. When he continued to defy me, I duplicated the subtraction. It is a standard penalty, Dumbledore, for such flagrant disobedience.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Removing house points is within your purview, Severus. The letter, however, speaks of cruelty, not discipline. Did the interaction end with the subtraction of points?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: It is the same matter, Dumbledore. I find it difficult to grasp how marking a student down for insubordination could be perceived as cruelty. It is a means to ensure the class runs smoothly and other students can learn without distraction. If the Longbottoms find that excessive, then perhaps the fault lies with their son's inability to follow simple instructions.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I am familiar with your classroom, Severus. I have observed the... atmosphere you cultivate. The governors' letter did not arise from a single instance of point removal. They speak of a pattern. Tell me, what was the nature of the 'mocking' you perceived? And what, precisely, did you say to Neville when you addressed him directly?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: The boy referred to me as a "foul git" under his breath. When I confronted him, I informed him that such language would not be tolerated and that further instances would result in detention. I stand by my actions. If that is considered 'cruelty' by today's standards, then I am guilty.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I see. And did you, at any point during this confrontation, make a comment regarding his magical aptitude? Or perhaps his family? The Longbottoms' letter suggests the reprimand was... personal in nature.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: If I made such a comment, it would have been in response to his continued defiance and insolence. It is not my intention to denigrate the Longbottoms or their son. However, it is my duty to hold him accountable for his actions and to prepare him for the realities of the magical world, which is often less forgiving than the protective environment of this school. If that offends the Longbottoms, so be it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Severus, your duty is to teach him Potions, not to prepare him for imagined cruelties by administering your own. The "realities of the magical world" do not excuse a professor from fostering a climate of fear. Did you, or did you not, make a remark about his parents' condition?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I do not recall making such a remark, Dumbledore. However, if I did, it was in the context of explaining why someone of his... disposition should not expect to be treated with kid gloves. It is my responsibility to ensure that students are ready for the rigors of the magical world, not to coddle them. If that is what you interpret as 'cruelty,' then I am at a loss to understand your expectations.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: My expectations are clear, Severus. They are the same for every member of this staff: to educate, not to terrorize. To challenge, not to crush. You speak of rigors, but you offer only humiliation. I will need a written account of the incident, and you will refrain from any further personal commentary directed at Mr. Longbottom. Is that understood?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand, Dumbledore. However, I must express my concern. By censuring me for my teaching methods, you risk sending a message that excellence is secondary to popularity. I will comply with your request, but I hope you will also address the issue of students' respect for their professors. It is a two-way street, after all.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Respect is earned, Severus, not demanded through intimidation. I will speak to Neville about his conduct. You will provide your account by tomorrow evening. And we will revisit this matter should the governors require more. That will be all.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: As you wish, Dumbledore. I will ensure that my account is thorough. I trust that you will also address the governors regarding the broader issue of discipline in the classroom. It seems that their concerns are not limited to my actions, but to the very nature of how we run our classes. Good evening, Headmaster.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Good evening, Severus. The nature of how we run our classes is indeed my concern. And it begins with ensuring every child feels safe enough to learn. We will speak again.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Safety? The path to true safety lies in preparation, not in pandering to the whims of delicate sensibilities. If you believe that by coddling these children, you are preparing them for the real world, then perhaps it is you who needs to be reprimanded, not I. Good evening, Dumbledore.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: That is enough, Severus. The conversation is concluded. Your account by tomorrow evening. Good night.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Good night, Headmaster. I will not keep you from your rest. I assume you will be addressing the rest of the staff on this matter, as well? It seems to me that the entire philosophy of education is under review. I will... adjust my methods accordingly. If that means pandering to the delicate sensibilities of these pampered brats, so be it.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: He dismisses alternative teaching philosophies as 'pandering to delicate sensibilities,' showing rigidity and resistance to new ideas.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: He emphasizes duty, accountability, and preparation, stating it is his 'responsibility to ensure that students are ready for the rigors of the magical world.'

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: He is confrontational and argumentative in a one-on-one setting, but shows no gregarious or sociable energy; his engagement is purely adversarial.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: He is openly antagonistic, blames the student and his family, and ends by calling students 'pampered brats,' showing very low compassion and cooperation.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: He reacts defensively and with hostility to criticism, perceiving the inquiry as a personal attack on his methods and authority.
